newsitem.title: INDIA: Naga separatists kill 30 passengers in India.
newsitem.headline: Naga separatists kill 30 passengers in India.

text.p: Separatist Naga tribal guerrillas shot dead 30 bus passengers and wounded 24 in the northeast Indian state of Nagaland near the Burmese border on Monday, police said.
Police officials in the state capital of Kohima told Reuters by telephone that the incident took place at Maiamnala, 105 km (65 miles) from Kohima.
Police said the guerrillas armed with guns and hand grenades stopped a bus carrying more than 60 passengers and asked ethnic Naga tribesmen to get off before opening fire on the others.
Police said all the dead were Kuki tribespeople, with whom the ethnic Nagas have a bitter rivalry.
Twenty-eight people were killed on the spot and two others died on the way to hospital, police said. At least 20 Naga guerrillas were involved in the incident, they added.
The wounded, six of whom were in serious condition, were admitted to hospital in nearby Dimapur town, where the bus had come from on its way to the rural centre of Jaluki, police said.
Dimapur is near the border of oil-rich Assam state, whose capital is Guwahati.
The Naga tribals have had a bloody feud with the Kukis since 1993, which has resulted in more than 1,000 deaths on both sides.

Indian officials say the two tribes are essentially fighting for control of a strategic drug trafficking route near the Burmese border. The route was once firmly under the control of Kukis before the Nagas laid claim to it, they say.
